messages:
maya: FYI customer reporting a spike of 502s during a nightly bulk embed job (~10k docs). Started after they migrated to our JS SDK v2. They see it mostly during the tail of the job when concurrency overlaps.

samir: Can you paste the minimal repro they gave? request IDs?

maya: They gave a short snippet and a stack trace. No single request ID but many proxied 502s from gateway. Repro (JS):
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, maxSockets: 10 }); // default
await client.embeddings.batch(docs, { batchSize: 64 });
```
They mentioned switching to keepAlive: true + default pooling caused an explosion of TIME_WAIT and then gateway returning 502s.

elaine: Any edge logs on our side showing connection limits / pool exhaustion?

opsbot: Incident created: INC-4892. Target sev: P2. Notifying eng-runtime.

samir: Looking at edge metrics now — we see a correlated spike in outbound ephemeral ports and 502 counters from the router at ~3334445600-3334445680. TCP closings in TIME_WAIT are high. Seems like client-side connection churn + our proxy limit on upstream connections.

maya: Customer says they run ~200 concurrent JS workers, each opens a small pool (maxSockets) so effective connections ~2000. SDK default maxSockets=10 is causing many short-lived sockets.

samir: Repro steps for us: run a harness that spawns 200 concurrent Node processes, each making 50 parallel embed requests (small payload). Watch edge router logs for 502 returns. I can push a local repro.

maya: They asked for a temporary mitigation to send them ASAP.

samir: Short-term mitigation options:
- Ask them to set maxSockets lower (1-2) at the process level and reuse a shared client instance instead of per-worker instantiation.
- Enable SDK option `agent.keepAlive: false` to avoid connection pooling if they can't centralize the client.
- We can increase upstream connection soft-limit on the gateway as a short-lived config (risk: higher memory).

maya: I proposed those to the customer: suggested single shared client per cluster + set maxSockets=2; customer wants us to try a server-side patch first.

samir: I'll prepare a conservative gateway config bump and a temporary per-route conn-limit increase for the customer's org-id. Rolling change, low-risk. Will also add verbose proxy connection logging for the window.

elaine: ETA?

samir: Doing canary now on eu-west-1 edge. If metrics look stable in 10m we'll roll to other regions. Patch includes: increase upstream_conn_limit from 1200 -> 3000 for org route, and enable "graceful-close-delay" to reduce TIME_WAIT buildup.

opsbot: Deploy job started: job-7742.

maya: Customer asked how we'll communicate status to them. Proposed message: "We identified excessive client-side connection churn with the new SDK; we are temporarily increasing upstream connection limits and recommend centralizing the SDK client. We'll follow up with a permanent fix and SDK patch." They want ETA ~30m.

samir: Update: canary looked good. 5xx rate dropped from 3.6% -> 0.2% in canary window. Rolling to other regions now.

elaine: Any long-term plan?

samir: Long-term: SDK patch to default to a shared global agent for common server setups, improved docs for multi-process deployments, and router heuristic to coalesce connections for high-cardinality orgs. I'll file ENG-rt-1227 for the SDK change.

maya: Customer notified with the canary numbers and recommended SDK changes. They replied :thumbsup: and asked for the SDK PR link and a follow-up once router heuristics are live.

opsbot: INC-4892 status -> monitoring. Assigned: samir.

jordan: Thanks team — I'll keep the customer posted and request logs if they see any further blips.

maya: Closing loop here after full rollout. Final note: we asked the customer to upgrade to SDK v2.1.3 (includes client reuse example) and to set maxSockets centrally.

samir: Marking follow-ups: ENG-rt-1227 (SDK default agent), ENG-oper-305 (router conn-coalesce).
